question: What is the deepest, vegetation-less and marshy area of a pond ecosystem called?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The profundal zone**__ .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **The deep zone** is the deepest region of the pond ecosystem, where sunlight does not reach.
 
• This area is **devoid of vegetation** because photosynthesis is not possible due to lack of light.
 
• **The amount of oxygen** is also low in this zone , due to which only certain types of organisms can survive.
 
• The deep zone is usually the site of the breakdown and decay of **mortal materials .**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The tropical zone**

 
 
• The tropical zone is the region which is located near the equator.
 
• The area is known for high temperatures and high humidity.
 
• There is a great diversity of plants and animals here.
 
• The region is generally known for its rainforests and areas of permanent moisture.
 
 
 
• **The temperate zone**
 
 
• The temperate zone is the region that lies between the tropical and polar regions.
 
• The region has four distinct seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter.
 
• The temperature and humidity here are moderate.
 
• A variety of ecosystems are found in the temperate zone, such as forests, grasslands, and lakes.
 
 
 
• **The lotic zone**
 
 
• The lotic zone is the area that contains bodies of flowing water, such as rivers and streams.
 
• There is a constant flow of water in this area, which increases the amount of oxygen.
 
• Various types of plants and animals are found here which can survive in flowing water.
 
• Water quality and transparency are very important in lotic ecosystems.
